lines.text: The tag lives in the wheel world, but the drive loop steers by the field pose. We need a bridge.
Step one: goal equals tag, composed with tag to goal. Rotate zero point six by one eighty degrees, and it points back at the robot.
With our tag, rounded, the goal is two point four, zero point six, facing zero degrees: right in front of the tag.
Step two: measure the goal from the wheel pose now, two point zero four, zero point five. Thirty six centimeters ahead, ten left.
Step three: hang that tape on the field pose, thirteen point three four, four point one. The field goal is thirteen point seven, four point two.
Together: the field goal is the field pose now, composed with the goal seen from the robot now.
Now a camera nudges the field pose three centimeters, to four point one three. The goal moves to four point two three. The gap is unchanged.
The drive loop only looks at that gap, so the jump cancels and the robot doesn't twitch.
And the map's goal? Thirteen point six seven, four point one seven. Four centimeters from the real spot: twice our whole budget.
